_comment: Tier 1 anomaly rules (ANALYTICS.md §3). CONFIG, not code: adding a rule is a data change. Every rule is a deterministic threshold or a baseline deviation — no LLM ever decides whether a rule fires. The `headline` is what a person reads; `observed`/`threshold` are what the engine computed, and both are kept on the event so any claim on screen can be traced to a number.

_schema.domain: weather | water | traffic | health | border | air | environment — Tier 2 groups by this
_schema.when.field: dot path into that source's trigger state, supports .length
_schema.when.value: numeric threshold, or number of SDs for the baseline ops
_schema.district_field: optional dot path to the district name, for Tier 2 convergence
_schema.converge: false to exclude this rule from Tier 2 grouping (default true)

rules._comment: The three rules below exist so every collected baseline signal is CONSUMED. collect_baselines.mjs folds four signals hourly; before these were added only longestWaitMin had a rule, so three quarters of the collection fed nothing — wasted work and a silent coverage gap. Each is aware of the (weekday, hour) bucket, which is the point: a queue that is normal at 08:00 Monday is not normal at 03:00 Sunday.
